questions.statement: Bogotá, ________ is the capital of Colombia, is home to many museums.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "That" cannot be used in non-defining clauses (after commas).
Correct! "Which" is used for non-defining clauses referring to places or things.
Incorrect. "Where" would be used if we described an action happening in the city, like "where I live".
Incorrect. For people.

questions.explanation:
En oraciones explicativas (entre comas), para referirnos a un objeto o lugar del que ya conocemos el nombre, usamos *which*.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The research team decided to avoid ________ animals in their cosmetic tests.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Avoid" is followed by a gerund.
Correct! Certain verbs like "avoid" always require the gerund form (-ing).
Incorrect. Incomplete form.
Incorrect. While grammatically okay, "using" is the expected verbal pattern.

questions.explanation:
Es fundamental recordar las regencias verbales: el verbo *avoid* siempre va seguido de un gerundio (*-ing*).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: We have ________ paint left, so we can't finish the mural today.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This would mean we have enough to continue.
Correct! "Little" indicates an insufficient amount (negative connotation).
Incorrect. "Paint" is uncountable.
Incorrect. For countable nouns.

questions.explanation:
El cuantificador *little* se usa con sustantivos incontables para expresar que la cantidad es poca e insuficiente.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ the new law, the citizens gathered in the square to celebrate.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The citizens didn't pass the law; the law was passed.
Correct! Active perfect participle for an action completed by the citizens.
Incorrect. Passive meaning.
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
El participio de perfecto (*Having heard*) indica que los ciudadanos se reunieron después de haber escuchado la noticia, estableciendo una secuencia lógica.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The explorer, ________ journal was found last year, disappeared in 1920.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Not referring to the explorer himself, but his journal.
Incorrect. For objects, but doesn't show possession.
Correct! "Whose" shows possession (the journal of the explorer).
Incorrect. Object form for people.

questions.explanation:
Usamos *whose* para conectar a una persona con algo que le pertenece en una oración de relativo.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The teacher gave ________ student a different topic to research.
questions.context: Identifying the correct quantifier for people.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Would require "all students".
Correct! "Each" refers to individuals in a group and takes a singular noun.
Incorrect. Not used for people in this way.
Incorrect. Implies only two students.

questions.explanation:
*Each* es el cuantificador ideal para resaltar la distribución individual de tareas o elementos entre los miembros de un grupo.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The scientist stopped ________ the sample because he noticed a contamination.
questions.context: Distinguishing meaning in gerund vs. infinitive.

options.feedback: Correct! "Stop + gerund" means ending the activity of analysis.
Incorrect. This would mean he made a pause in another activity *to start* analyzing.
Incorrect. Incomplete form.
Incorrect. Grammatically wrong.

questions.explanation:
A nivel B2, es vital distinguir el cambio de significado con el verbo *stop*: el gerundio indica el fin de la acción que se estaba realizando.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ by the beautiful landscape, the artist decided to stay for another week.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This would mean the artist was inspiring someone else.
Correct! Past participle clause shows the passive cause of the artist's decision.
Incorrect. Active meaning.
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
Usamos el participio pasado (*Inspired*) para describir cómo se siente el sujeto o qué le ha afectado, funcionando como una causa pasiva ("Because he was inspired...").

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: In which sentence can the relative pronoun be **removed**?

options.text: The hotel which has the best reviews is expensive.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Which" is the subject.

options.text: The tour which I booked was excellent.
options.feedback: Correct! "Which" is the object of "booked".

options.text: The guide, who was very kind, spoke four languages.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Cannot omit in non-defining clauses.

options.text: The museum whose director I met is closed today.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Whose" is never omitted.

questions.explanation:
Solo podemos omitir el pronombre relativo en oraciones especificativas cuando este funciona como objeto de la cláusula subordinada.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Identify the error in this paragraph:
"Innovation involves **to take** (A) risks. Every **scientist** (B) knows that. The laboratory **where** (C) we work is well-equipped, providing **all** (D) the necessary tools."
questions.context: Finding an error in a summary text.

options.feedback: Correct! "Involve" must be followed by a gerund: "involves taking".
Incorrect. "Every" is correctly followed by a singular noun.
Incorrect. Correct use for place.
Incorrect. Correct use for uncountable "tools" (or countable plural).

questions.explanation:
El verbo *involve* (involucrar) requiere gramaticalmente un gerundio (*-ing*), no un infinitivo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is the most formal way to describe a historical artifact?

options.text: We found an artifact that was buried in the sand.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Simple relative clause.

options.text: Found in the sand, the artifact was taken to the museum.
options.feedback: Correct! Uses a participle clause for a formal and concise tone.

options.text: The artifact was found in the sand and people took it to the museum.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Too informal.

options.text: Having found in the sand, the artifact went to the museum.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Grammatically wrong (active perfect participle).

questions.explanation:
Las oraciones de participio son una marca de registro formal en inglés, permitiendo una transición fluida entre la descripción de un objeto y la acción que se realizó con él.

questions.statement:
Choose the most coherent summary:
"The museum, ________ houses rare artifacts, attracts ________ visitor every day. ________ by the past, people continue ________ the secrets of our history."
questions.context: Choosing the best integration of grammar.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "That" after comma.
Correct! Proper use of relative pronoun, quantifier, participle and gerund.

options.text: where / all / Having inspired / to study
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Where" needs a subject and verb following.
Incorrect. "Study" needs -ing or to.

questions.explanation: Este ejercicio final evalúa la integración de cuatro puntos gramaticales clave del nivel B2 en un solo contexto narrativo sobre cultura e historia.
